I read the diff. I could not run `tsc` or Biome, because `node_modules` is not installed and running the tools needs approval. These candidates come from reading the code only.

tsconfig.check.json:7 | `"rootDir": "."` removes the check that `src` stays inside the build's `rootDir: "src"`. The old CI step, `tsc --noEmit` on `tsconfig.json`, reported TS6059 for a `src` file that imports from outside `src`. Now only `npm run build` catches it, and that runs only in the `publish` job on a `v*` tag. | A `src/*.ts` file that imports `../tests/helpers.js` or any other file outside `src`. The quality job passes on the branch and on `main`, and the release fails after the tag is pushed. Nothing in `src` does this today.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:28 | The quality job no longer type-checks with the build config (`tsconfig.json`) at all. Any error that only the build config gives now shows up first at publish. This is the broader form of the finding above. | Any option in `tsconfig.json` that the check config overrides or changes, now or later (`rootDir`, `include`/`exclude`), and that makes `tsc` fail. Today the only such option is `rootDir`.
tsconfig.check.json:1 | The new file starts with `//` comments. `npx biome check --error-on-warnings` in the Lint step also reads JSON files. If Biome does not parse `tsconfig.check.json` as JSONC, it reports a parse error and Lint fails. | Biome 2.x reads `tsconfig.check.json` without comments allowed. I am not sure: Biome allows comments in `tsconfig.json`, and I think it also allows them in `tsconfig.*.json`, but I did not check this. The repository has no `biome.json` that sets it.
tsconfig.check.json:4 | Through `extends`, `"declaration": true` now applies to `tests/` too. So `tsc` also checks declaration emit for the test files, and an exported test helper without an explicit return type can give TS4xxx/TS2742 errors that the build never shows. | A test helper exported with an inferred type that cannot be named, for example a vitest mock type. `tests/helpers.ts` gives `fakeFetch` an explicit return type, so nothing sets this off today.
